steps.text: Place butter, cream cheese, sour cream, flour, and salt in a food processor; pulse until crumbly.
Shape and press crumbly dough mixture into four equal disks. Wrap each pastry disk; chill in the refrigerator for 1 hour or up to 2 days.
Combine walnuts, raisins, sugar, and cinnamon in a bowl.

Roll each pastry disk into a 9-inch round keeping other disks chilled until ready to roll them. Sprinkle round with walnut-raisin mixture; press lightly into dough. Cut each round into 12 wedges with a chefs knife or pizza cutter. Roll wedges from wide to narrow, you will end up with point on outside of cookie. Place on ungreased baking sheets and chill rugelach for 20 minutes before baking.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (180 degrees C).
After rugelach are chilled, bake in the preheated oven on center rack until lightly golden, about 22 to 25 minutes; cool on wire racks.

raw_recipe.headline: Rugelach
raw_recipe.description: Rugelach are crescent-shaped pastries that are easy to make at home with flaky dough and a sweet walnut-raisin filling for a delicious Jewish holiday treat.

video.description:
In this video, discover a homemade Rugelach recipe. These pastries feature a buttery pastry enveloping a classic filling of walnuts, raisins, sugar, and cinnamon. You can customize your creation with chocolate or your favorite jam. This straightforward recipe promises a delectable taste experience.

Crafted with simple ingredients like all-purpose flour, cream cheese, sour cream, and butter, these Rugelach require just 2 hours and 25 minutes to make. Create your batch of Rugelach and enjoy the rich, timeless flavors that have been cherished for generations. Share these delightful pastries with your loved ones.

review.reviewBody:
These were a huge hit at the office. For anyone who is having issues with filling falling out, I would suggest pushing the chunky parts of the filling to the outside of the circle (leaving the cinnamon/sugar mixure in the middle) before rolling. This way you can squeeze the raisins/nuts in as you roll.

Also if you don't want to make the crescent shape, you can use this recipe to make roulades (exactly the same cookie, just a cinnamon roll-like shape). To do this, roll the dough out either into a rectangle or circle. Then add the toppings. Roll the dough with the filling. Then cut into 1 inch pieces. (Note: If you rolled into a circle, you'll need to cut a 1/4 inch piece off of each end before cutting the 1 inch cookie pieces.) Place seam side down for baking.

This is the first time I've ever made rugelach--and it will not be the last!! Jackie, your recipe is awesome! I am amazed at how the rugelach dough comes out almost like a phyllo dough--it's layered and almost laminated; but without all that extra work! My only changes to the recipe were to add 1 tbsp sugar to the dough; and I toasted the walnuts before grinding them for the filling. I left out the raisins, and used brown sugar. I also egg washed the rugelach before baking to get a nice golden brown color to them. Finally, my rugelach needed about 30 minutes bake time to be fully done. I really enjoyed the process of making these--and how delicious they were when done! It was a fight to keep my hubby out of them! Thank you so much for sharing your recipe!

This is without a doubt the absolute best recipe I have ever used to make these!!!!! I use seedless raspberry jam and mini chocolate chips for filling and use the back of a spoon to lightly press the chips into the dough. Instead of rolling into a circle, I roll this into a rectangle, add filling, and then cut in half and then cut in strips and roll them. Less filling comes out and it is much easier and less mess.

Oh, boy! I love making Rugelach, and this recipe is a winner! I didn't have sour cream, so I substituted plain Greek yogurt. I had leftover homemade almond paste, so I rolled it into two large discs for filling half of these dough circles, and added chopped almonds. For the remaining two dough discs, I used the traditional cinnamon-sugar mixture with chopped walnuts. I have always brushed my dough with melted butter before adding nuts and cinnamon-sugar, and I noticed this recipe doesn't include that. No matter... these baked up beautifully and I love the tips about rolling the cinnamon sugar into the dough and then chilling the filled rugelach before baking. Awesome! This will replace my old tattered Rugelach recipe from now on.

this recipe is the easiest and most fun recipe to do!! my son was doing a country project and he chose Israel. I went searching for a pastry recipe and came across this recipe. I can say I've needed to watch myself not eat it all. I don't have a food processor so I used my hands to mix it all in, but I found the best way to keep the batter on point is to use butter that is either frozen or just out of the refrigerator. my sour cream, cream cheese, and butter were all cold and ready to mix, and after I mixed I placed round sections of batter in saran wrap just like it says in the instructions, and then I let it sit in the fridge for a couple of hours while I'm doing other things around the house and when I'm ready to roll out the dough then I get my cookie sheet ready for all the last steps and once they are all rolled onto the cookie sheet I leave it in the fridge overnight so I can bake them fresh in the morning for my kids to take for school snack. it cooks exactly 25 min and it's the best they have ever tasted. For the kids I only up sugar and cinnamon inside. thank you for sharing this amazing recipe, it will be forever in our family

This was my first time making rugelach, and they turned out great! I made the dough exactly as stated, but brushed it with apricot jam prior to adding the walnut/sugar mixture. I omitted the raisins and added brown sugar. I filled half with a poppyseed filling. I brushed the tops with egg wash and sprinkled with sanding sugar. Absolutely delicious!! Will be making again.

Got this recipe in my email and thought "that sounds good" so I made a test batch this week in anticipation of taking to my daughters house Christmas morning.

I'm too lazy to make the dough, and after reading about cutting the disks into wedges, I thought "canned crescent rolls" will make an easy substitute, and they did!

I combined white sugar, brown sugar, cinnamon, and chopped walnuts and set aside in a small bowl. Opened the crescent rolls, and sprinkled them liberally with the sugar/nut mixture. On a few, I spread some peach preserves.

After baking about 14 minutes, I cut each roll into thirds and these little treats were fantastic. These were gobbled up by 3 of us in 15 minutes!

Can't wait for Christmas morning.

This is a great recipe, and while a little time consuming, it's not difficult at all. I liked the comment about rolling out in a sugar mixture. I was worried about the ragged edge when rolling the dough out, but that takes care of itself. Also, I did part of them with apricot spread from Whole Foods and it helped the mixture stick to the dough. Also, I put a piece of waxed paper down and rolled the mixture lightly to press into the dough. I will chill the rolled dough longer than 20 minutes the next time. My second pan, which chilled for 30-40 minutes came out better. I also baked the cookies for 24 minutes.

Was surprised how easy the dough was to make and how far the dough went. I got about 70 rugelach out the dough. They were a huge hit and I'll be making them again and experimenting with fillings. I made half with cinnamon/raisin/hazelnut and other half with raspberry jam (heated in micro with 1 tbsp sugar), dark choc and hazel nuts. And I definitely recommend doing an egg wash on the rolled rugelach otherwise they look dull.

DELISH! I've made them with a) sugar/cinnamon/walnuts/mini dark-chocolate chips, b) Solo apricot filling/walnuts (or almonds)/cinnamon, c) Solo raspberry filling/dark chocolate chips. (A) and (B) are *wonderful* --- wasn't crazy about (C). Also, after the 1st time I made this recipe, I stopped cutting the prepared dough into wedges and rolling --- now I just roll the entire thing into a 'log' and slice into pieces about 1 1/2" wide. This works *much* better for me and the filling doesn't fall out! I brush the top of each piece with beaten egg and drop into either a sugar/cinnamon mix or into crushed nuts before baking.

Excellent, authentic recipe, just like you get on the East Coast. MAKE IT EASIER! 1) SKIP 2-HOUR CHILLING! Instead, I sandwiched a ball of dough between 2 pieces of saran wrap, rolled to 9" round, peeled off the top layer of plastic, placed fillings, cut with pizza cutter and was ready to go! 2)FRESH ANYTIME: This dough refrigerates VERY well so you might as well make the whole recipe, refrig until needed, and then bake as much as suits your household. OTHER TIPS: 1) Choco filling: 1 cup chocolate chips (chopped) tossed with 1/2 cup white sugar, fill as usual. 2) after making your rolled crescents, chill for 10-20min in the fridge so they maintain the pretty shape while baking. this is optional, but easy if you skipped 2h of chilling.
the combo of sour cream and cream cheese causes perfection

I made these for the first time this Christmas and we loved them. My recommendations would be to make the four discs of dough then put in the freezer until the next day or so. Bake day let thaw the night before in the refrigerator. Be sure and roll out dough to recommended thickness or diameter. If too thick and it will take longer to bake the dough rolls all the way through. I also brushed the disc lightly with jam before adding and gently packing the finely chopped pecans, cinnamon and sugar mixture. No raisins for me.

My mom used to make these after have bought some at the Public Market & the farmer's market & falling in love with them. But I think she made them either with crescent roll dough or ready made pie crusts & they were delicious!!! And took a lot less time & work! Boy, do I miss my mom! 😘💟

There was so much stuff that it barely fit in my full sized food processor. I have double-checked and yes, I used the proper amounts of ingredients. It never crumbled in the food processor. I see in one of the comments that they made sure the butter, etc, were very cold. I wish I'd known that, I brought it all to room temperature. The dough waited to crumble until after I took it out of the fridge the next day and tried to roll it out. I ended up with a "crumble", not a cookie. I wasn't impressed.

This recipe was awesome! It's important though to mention that the butter and cream cheese should be very cold. I put mine in the freezer for 15 minutes while I prepared all the other ingredients. I also added currants and Walnuts, and spread lightly with jam .

Terrific recipe. Was surprised by how flaky the dough turned out. I did not have a stand mixer and so used a hand mixer to cut everything down. I was worried about the chunks of butter still visible in the discs but it turned out all right. I did this in two batches. I used a thicker layer of jam in the first one and it spilled out and stuck to the baking sheet. (Still delish though). For the second one I used a thinner layer of jam and worked the dough more while rolling it out and they came out great.

Easy to make. My only change was to not add the sour cream to the dough. Instead, I brushed the rolled out dough with the sour cream, sprinkled the topping over (and yes, with chocolate chips!) press the filling gently into the dough and follow the rest of the directions.

This was my first time making rugelach! And this was the only online recipe that wasn't 3 out of 5 stars so I was a bit nervous. I used the whisk attachment on my pro 5 (I don't have a processor) and the dough came out perfect. I did one batch raisin and one mini chocolate chip.
